newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen, Veba want Vulkan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen, Veba want Vulkan - paper.

text.p: Germany's leading financial daily reported on Wednesday that Duesseldorf-based companies Thyssen AG and Veba AG were interested in taking over bankrupt shipyard group Bremer Vulkan Verbund AG.

Handelsblatt said in a front-page story that, despite publicly distancing themselves from takeover speculation, the two companies wanted to pick up loss carryovers worth between three and four billion marks to cut their own tax exposure.

The newspaper also quoted informed sources saying that the two potential buyers wanted to dampen takeover talk to prevent shares in Bremer Vulkan -- which are still listed -- from jumping further after their price trebled on Monday.
Bremer Vulkan shares surged to 9.90 marks from 3.44 marks last Friday, but fell back to close on Tuesday at 5.10 marks.

That is a tiny fraction of the share price of around 80 marks at which they were trading before the Bremen shipbuilder collapsed a year ago after it emerged that managers had misused European Union industrial subsidies to prop up the company.
Thyssen on Tuesday denied a report in the Weser Kurier, a Bremen newspaper, that it wanted to buy Vulkan.

Ulrich Noelle, finance senator for the city state, confirmed at the weekend that he was talking to two potential buyers. Handelsblatt said in its report, however, that Noelle had distanced himself from such plans.

The report said Thyssen, which is pursuing a strategy to refocus on its core steel and engineering, was planning to sell its E-Plus mobile telephone unit -- a move which would lead to sizeable extraordinary earnings.

To cut its tax exposure, Thyssen could offset the windfall gain from the E-Plus sale through the Vulkan loss carryover. Telecommunications venture o.tel.o, which is owned by utilities Veba and RWE AG, has been named as a potential buyer for E-Plus.
One member of the committee of creditors to Vulkan, Joerg Stein, told Handelsblatt that a sale of the group to the two potential buyers would be "sensible, wise and achievable".
